To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

TnT is a novel transcription factor that interacts with the p53 pathway and that TnT expression is down‐regulated in aged skeletal muscle, contributing to muscle insulin resistance and possibly &bgr;‐cell dysfunction.

the nuclear pool of fast skeletal muscle TnT3 interacts with p53 binding sites in the promoter areas of p53‐regulated genes, including the p53‐inducibile RRM2B gene, which is involved in DNA synthesis and replication.

the fast skeletal muscle TnT3 protein shuttles between the cytoplasm and the nucleus, where its fragments associate with DNA consensus sequence, which overlaps with p53‐binding motifs, suggesting that TnT2‐3 may contribute to age‐ and disease‐related muscle wasting by modulating the expression of p53‐dependent genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of TnT in muscle aging.
a non‐canonical function of the skeletal muscle TnT3 in regulating the expression of p53‐regulated genes.

the discovery of a novel function of TnT and its fragments in the nucleus and their contribution to age‐related muscle wasting and other age‐related conditions such as insulin resistance and β‐cell dysfunction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TnT isoforms are not only important in muscle contraction but they are also involved in muscle homeostasis and muscle aging.
TnT is a multifunctional protein with cytoplasmic and nuclear roles in the regulation of muscle function and aging.
TnT is an emerging player in age‐related sarcopaenia and other age‐related diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TnT‐binding sites are located in the promoter area and intronic regions of genes that are involved in muscle function, muscle insulin resistance, muscle wasting and muscle aging.
TnT is a novel transcriptional regulator of p53‐mediated genes, which may contribute to age‐ and obesity‐related sarcopenic and insulin‐resistant states.
reduced expression of the TNNT3 gene is one of the mechanisms leading to sarcopenia and other age‐related muscle and metabolic disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that

TnT is not only a structural component of the thin filament, but also a transcriptional regulatory protein that may play an important role in the development and progression of muscle wasting and insulin resistance with aging.
